cells.value: Personal Data Protection Law No. 151/2020 in force since October 2020; Executive Regulations issued by Decree No. 816/2025 of the Minister of Communications and Information Technology on 1 November 2025, published in the Official Gazette on 1 November 2025 and effective the following day; Personal Data Protection Centre (PDPC) operationalised as supervisory authority (official site pdpc.gov.eg live, Executive Regulations text and initial guidance published December 2025); one-year transitional grace period for controllers/processors ends 1 November 2026, so no enforcement track record yet; mandatory licensing/permit regime, DPO registry with PDPC-approved exams, and 72-hour breach notification defined in the Regulations; electronic licensing portal expected to open around mid-2026.
cells.source_title: Shalakany Law Office, "New Executive Regulations for Egypt's Personal Data Protection Law" (Dec 2025) — full-text analysis of Decree 816/2025
cells.tier: T4 (law-firm full-text analyses; T3 anchor = Official Gazette Decree 816/2025 and pdpc.gov.eg, which lack resolvable public deep links — see protocol_issues)
cells.quality_evidence: Executive Regulations issued (Decree 816/2025, Gazette 1 Nov 2025) after a five-year gap — the enforcement machinery now exists: PDPC established under PDPL Art. 19 (affiliated to MCIT) with licensing/permit powers, DPO registry and exams, 72-hour breach notification, cross-border transfer rules, children's-data and direct-marketing rules. Enforcement itself is deferred: one-year grace period to 1 Nov 2026; licensing portal expected ~mid-June 2026. The regime transitions to Operating when PDPC licensing/enforcement begins after the grace period.
cells.search_trail: Searched: (1) web search 'PDPL 151/2020 executive regulations status 2025 Data Protection Centre' -> T4 law-firm and privacy-monitor coverage (Baker McKenzie, Al Tamimi, Kennedys, Clyde&Co, Lexis ME, DataGuidance); (2) T3 official: pdpc.gov.eg (resolves 200, JS app, no deep links), mcit.gov.eg news 63220 (Mar 2021 draft-regs consultation), SIS ratification page (2020); Official Gazette issue not publicly deep-linkable; (3) Arabic search 'اللائحة التنفيذية قانون حماية البيانات قرار 816' -> Masaar full text (403 to direct fetch), law-firm summaries; settled on Shalakany full-text PDF (resolves 200, Wayback capture requested 2026-08-22) + DataGuidance.
cells.notes: MAJOR UPDATE vs prior desk pass: prior recorded PDPL as in force with executive regulations pending (record stale, year 2020). Regulations have now been issued (1 Nov 2025) and the PDPC stood up — the prior's main caveat is resolved, though enforcement only begins after 1 Nov 2026. Minor source conflicts noted: one Kluwer/Lexis piece calls Decree 816/2025 a Prime Ministerial decree, while full-text sources (Shalakany, Al Tamimi, Masaar) attribute it to the Minister of CIT — the latter is followed here; grace-period end reported variously as 31 Oct 2026 and 1 Nov 2026.
cells.protocol_issues: T3 primary artefact (Official Gazette text of Decree 816/2025) has no stable public deep link; PDPC official site is a JavaScript SPA whose root resolves but exposes no citable document URLs — presence facts therefore rest on archived T4 full-text law-firm analyses. Flag for Katreyna: whether reputable law-firm client briefings reproducing gazetted text should be treated as T3-equivalent for legal presence facts.

cells.source_title: ITU Global Cybersecurity Index 2024 (5th edition) — Egypt in Tier 1 'Role-modelling' (score band 95-100); exact score 100/100 per NTRA announcement
cells.tier: T1 (ITU report) + T3 (NTRA, Egypt's telecom regulator, for the exact 100-point figure)
cells.search_trail: Searched: (1) ITU GCI 2024 report PDF (T1) — downloaded and text-extracted: Egypt listed in 'Tier performance: Global' under Tier 1 - Role-modelling (score of 95-100), p.23 annex, and in 'Tier Performance: Arab States' Tier 1, p.27; report publishes tiers, not per-country overall scores; (2) ITU DataHub indicator 90014 'GCI Overall Score' for EGY (T1) — blocked, HTTP 403 via direct fetch, API and in-browser session on 2026-08-22; (3) NTRA (T3, 18 Sep 2024): Egypt among only 12 countries scoring 100 points, of 47 Tier-1 countries; EG-CERT (T3) corroborates.
cells.notes: Value expressed on the indicator's 0-1 scale: GCI 2024 score 100/100 = 1.00 (prior 2020 edition: 95.48). Verifies the prior desk pass (100, Tier 1, level 5). Egypt is one of 12 countries with a perfect score in GCI 2024.
cells.protocol_issues: Two flags: (a) indicator is specified 0-1 but ITU publishes GCI on 0-100 — recorded 1.0 with the 100/100 basis stated; confirm the intended normalisation in the spec. (b) The GCI 2024 report itself publishes tier bands only (95-100 for Tier 1); the exact per-country score sits in ITU DataHub, which returned HTTP 403 to all access routes at capture time — the exact '100' therefore rests on the national regulator's announcement (T3), with the T1 report confirming the 95-100 band. Either reading clears the top threshold (>=0.8).

cells.source_title: Oxford Insights Government AI Readiness Index 2024 — Full rankings annex: Egypt total 55.63 (Government 68.98, Technology Sector 42.13, Data & Infrastructure 55.77)
cells.search_trail: Searched: (1) Oxford Insights GAIRI 2025 report PDF (T4 primary) — downloaded and text-extracted: Egypt rank 51 of 195 with pillar scores Policy Capacity 100.00, AI Infrastructure 46.06, Governance 62.50, Public Sector Adoption 60.07, Development & Diffusion 45.41, Resilience 62.81; the 2025 annex does NOT print overall country scores; (2) oxfordinsights.com downloads page — Index Data file gated behind a registration form, no open deep link; OxfordInsights GitHub repo holds only legacy 2019-methodology data; (3) GAIRI 2024 report PDF (T4 primary) 'Full rankings' annex pp.42-44 — Egypt overall 55.63, verified in extracted text; (4) press (Egypt Today/SIS, T5/not admissible) reports 2025 overall score 57.5, rank 51, 1st in Africa.
cells.notes: Scored value is the openly verifiable 2024-edition figure (55.63). The 2025 edition places Egypt 51st of 195 (up from 65th), 1st in Africa, with a widely reported overall score of 57.5 — but the 2025 report PDF omits overall scores and the underlying data file is registration-gated, so 57.5 could not be verified against an admissible open source. Both 55.63 and 57.5 fall in the same 40-60 threshold band, so the level implication is unchanged. Divergence from prior: prior recorded 57.5 (2025) — plausible and consistent with press, but not source-verifiable; replaced with the verifiable 55.63 (2024) and the 2025 facts carried in notes.
cells.protocol_issues: Latest-edition (2025) exact overall score is not resolvable to an open primary source (report prints ranks + pillar scores only; data file behind a form). Flag for the ledger: refresh this cell if Oxford Insights publishes the open 2025 data file, and decide whether rank+pillar scores from the primary PDF outrank a press-reported overall score.

cells.value: No dedicated national digital agriculture strategy identified as of August 2026. Digital agriculture exists as components inside broader frameworks: (a) the updated Sustainable Agricultural Development Strategy (SADS 2030) — MALR's assistant minister stated in June 2021 that digital transformation was incorporated into Egypt's updated agriculture strategy and that MALR created a Digital Transformation Unit for the first time; (b) the Digital Egypt agenda — a defined MALR-MCIT joint project portfolio (agriculture services on the Digital Egypt platform, automated agricultural tenure, farmer card, satellite/AI crop identification, Hudhud smart assistant); (c) the National AI Strategy 2nd edition (2025-2030), which names agriculture a strategic sector; plus an FAO-MALR agricultural digital transformation programme (2018-2022).
cells.source_title: MCIT press release, 'ICT Minister, Agriculture Minister follow up on joint digital transformation projects', 9 June 2021
cells.quality_evidence: Not applicable to a dedicated strategy (none exists). The embedded digital-ag agenda has institutional carriers: MALR Digital Transformation Unit (created 2021), the MALR-MCIT joint project portfolio, and SADS 2030 (FAOLEX text; updated executive summary Dec 2020).
cells.search_trail: Searched: (1) FAO e-agriculture / FAOLEX (T1/T3) — no Egypt national e-agriculture strategy; FAO-Egypt digital extension programme 2018-2022 only; (2) T3 official: mcit.gov.eg press room (2020/2021 joint-project releases), sis.gov.eg strategy pages (Food Security Strategy — not digital-ag), moa.gov.eg e-services; (3) Arabic search 'استراتيجية التحول الرقمي في الزراعة / الزراعة الرقمية 2025' — plans and project reviews only, no adopted dedicated strategy; (4) T2: ICARDA/CGSpace 'Current Situation of Digital Agriculture in Egypt' (2023, limited access — landing page silent on a strategy); (5) T4: World Bank DigitalAG4Egypt — an innovation competition, not a strategy.
cells.notes: Divergence from prior: prior filled this cell with 'SADS 2030' (level 3, stale 2020). Verified honestly: SADS 2030 is the general agriculture strategy with digital transformation incorporated in its update — there is no dedicated national digital agriculture strategy, announced or adopted. No 2025-26 development toward one was found (the Jan 2025 AI strategy and Dec 2025 ministerial statements reference digital-ag projects, not a sector digital strategy).
cells.protocol_issues: Indicator definition ambiguity: Egypt sits between rungs — a dedicated digital-ag strategy is Absent, while digital-ag components are adopted and operating inside SADS 2030 / Digital Egypt / NAIS-2. Recorded Absent (dedicated reading) with embedded components documented; the scoring convention for embedded-strategy cases should be fixed in the spec.

cells.value: No agricultural data governance framework (sector-specific rules on agricultural data sharing, ownership or use) identified — refutation attempt failed. The general PDPL 151/2020 and its Executive Regulations (Decree 816/2025) now govern personal data, including farmers' personal data, but contain no agriculture-specific provisions. MALR operates large farmer databases (electronic tenure registry, farmer card) with no published data-sharing/ownership rules; the OECD's comprehensive 2025 review of Egyptian agricultural policy documents no ag-data governance instrument.
cells.source_title: OECD, Policies for the Future of Farming and Food in Egypt (agricultural policy review — no agricultural data governance instrument appears)
cells.tier: T2 (OECD review) + T4 (PDPL ER analysis); absence finding as of 2026-08-22
cells.search_trail: Refutation attempt, in tier order: (1) T1/T2: World Bank open-data blog on farmer data policy (generic, no Egypt instrument), OECD Egypt agricultural policy review (T2 — no data-governance framework), FAO Egypt Country Programming Framework; (2) T3: FAOLEX SADS 2030 text, PDPL 151/2020 + Executive Regulations 816/2025 (general, no ag carve-out), moa.gov.eg services pages; (3) English and Arabic web searches 'Egypt agricultural data governance / farmer data sharing rules ownership MALR' — only academic proposals (arXiv) and non-Egypt codes of conduct surfaced. Nothing announced or adopted found.
cells.notes: Prior desk pass: Absent (level 2 'narrow presence' via general PDPL). Verified: still Absent as a sector framework. One material change since the prior: the PDPL Executive Regulations (Nov 2025) now give the general regime real machinery (licensing, breach notification), which strengthens the horizontal baseline that would underpin any future ag-data rules — but nothing sector-specific exists. AGI prerequisite accordingly remains unmet on the sector-specific reading.
cells.protocol_issues: Recording convention: this is a verified absence (a valid finding), not a data gap — value_type 'citation' used with the refutation trail rather than 'gap', since the search was conclusive across tiers. Confirm this convention in the spec for prerequisite-absence cells.

cells.value: Egypt National AI Strategy, 2nd edition (2025-2030), unveiled January 2025 (1st edition 2021), explicitly includes agriculture: named among strategic sectors for AI integration ('agriculture, manufacturing, defense, education, cybersecurity, smart cities, and healthcare'); a dedicated Agriculture use-case cluster (prediction of pest & disease outbreaks, pest/disease recognition, Virtual Farmer Advisor chatbot, crop mapping and yield prediction, crop optimization 'grow what where', smart water management); agriculture is a named key-industry domain (L1 model) in the national Arabic LLM development programme; the Agriculture Research Center is listed among implementing stakeholders.
cells.source_title: Egypt National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, Second Edition 2025-2030 (official English text, ai.gov.eg, 16 Jan 2025)
cells.quality_evidence: Governance: National Council for Artificial Intelligence (formed 2019) oversees the strategy; strategy structured on six pillars with named institutional owners; unveiled by the President (Jan 2025). Continuity: 2nd edition builds on the 2021 first edition, under which MCIT's Applied Innovation Center ran agriculture pilots with the Agriculture Research Center (AIC-ARC AI pilot referenced in the Sept 2020 MCIT-MALR ministerial meeting) that produced deployed tools (Hudhud pest-ID, satellite/AI crop mapping).
cells.scale_evidence: Agriculture-relevant deployments delivered under the strategy's first edition are recorded in bundle E1 cells (Hudhud, crop mapping); no agriculture-specific budget line is published in the strategy PDF.
cells.search_trail: Searched: (1) T3 official: ai.gov.eg strategy PDF (downloaded, full-text verified for agriculture content — hits at strategic-sector lists, agriculture use-case table, LLM key-industry table, ARC stakeholder list); (2) T4: Digital Watch Observatory resource page, OECD.AI policy dashboard entry, Regulations.AI entries (1st and 2nd editions); (3) Oxford Insights GAIRI 2025 (T4) independently notes Egypt 'released a new and updated version of its AI strategy' following its first strategy.
cells.notes: Verifies and strengthens the prior desk pass (prior: 2nd edition names agriculture as a Phase 1 priority, level 4). Precise verified framing: agriculture appears as a strategic sector, a named use-case cluster, and an LLM domain — the exact phrase 'Phase 1 priority sector' was not located in the extracted text; the substance of the prior claim stands.

cells.source_title: World Bank Identification for Development (ID4D) Data — ID ownership, total (% of population ages 15+), Egypt, 2024 observation: 98.78 (API value 98.7781785562663; source 89, indicator ID.OWN.TOTL.ZS; 2025 dataset update based on the Global Findex 2024 survey round)
cells.search_trail: Searched: (1) T1 machine-fetch: World Bank API source 89 (ID4D) — ID.OWN.TOTL.ZS for EGY returns 2024 = 98.778, 2021 = 97.315; (2) T1 document: ID4D Global Dataset Volume 1 (2021 estimates), appendix p.43 — Egypt National ID Card (بطاقة الرقم القومي), age 16+: 2021 total 97.3 (women 97.7, men 96.9); 2017 total 93.7; (3) checked for newer sources: ID4D 2025 update confirmed (leverages Findex 2024 round) via id4d.worldbank.org/global-dataset and World Bank blog.
cells.notes: Refreshed and corrected vs prior. Prior recorded 97.2% (2021, 'World Bank ID4D') — 97.2 matches the 2017 men's column of the ID4D table, an apparent mis-read; the correct 2021 total was 97.3%. Updated to the 2024 observation: 98.8% of adults (15+) own the national ID — comfortably above the top threshold (80). FIN prerequisite satisfied. Single-source in the strict sense (ID4D/Findex is the sole survey series) but triangulated across vintages (2017: 93.7 -> 2021: 97.3 -> 2024: 98.8) within the T1 database; no independent second T1 source exists for this construct.
cells.protocol_issues: Note the construct: ID4D measures ownership of the national ID card (foundational ID), not a digital/online ID; Egypt's ID4D digital-ID indicator ('have online digital ID') is a separate series. Indicator 4.7 as named ('Digital ID coverage') is satisfied here by foundational-ID coverage per the prior convention — confirm intended construct in the spec.

cells.value: No gazetted standing inter-ministerial committee for digital agriculture identified; what exists and is documented is a continuous de facto coordination mechanism between MALR and MCIT: recurring joint ministerial review meetings (23 Sept 2020 on AI for agriculture; 9 June 2021 follow-up on a defined joint project portfolio — agriculture services on Digital Egypt platform, automated agricultural tenure, farmer card issuance, satellite/AI crop identification, Hudhud smart assistant, e-archive); a dedicated MALR Digital Transformation Unit created (2021) as institutional counterpart; multi-agency delivery including the Egyptian Survey Authority and Ministry of Planning on the agricultural tenure digitization; and continued cooperation affirmed by the Agriculture Minister in December 2025.
cells.source_title: MCIT press release, 9 June 2021 — ICT and Agriculture Ministers follow up on joint digital transformation projects (portfolio listed; MALR digital transformation unit created)
cells.quality_evidence: Continuity across five-plus years and across a change of agriculture minister (El Quseir 2020-21 meetings -> Farouk Dec 2025 statement on digital transformation successes); institutionalised counterpart (MALR Digital Transformation Unit, first created 2021); delivery footprint spans additional agencies (Egyptian Survey Authority agricultural tenure project page names MALR and Ministry of Planning cooperation). Weakness: no decree, published terms of reference, or standing-committee mandate found — the mechanism is recurring bilateral ministerial review, not a constituted body.
cells.scale_evidence: Joint outputs at national scale are documented in other cells (farmer card/Meeza registry, tenure automation, Hudhud). Press reporting citing MALR (agrinewz, June 2026 — T5, narrative only, not admissible for a scored value) puts electronic agricultural tenure records at ~5.2 million holdings with a database covering 7+ million feddans.
cells.search_trail: Searched: (1) T3 official: mcit.gov.eg press room (releases 50862 of 23 Sept 2020 and 63422 of 9 June 2021 — both fetched and read; neither names a standing committee), sis.gov.eg (27 Dec 2025 Agriculture Minister statement — fetched), esa.gov.eg agricultural tenure project page (fetched); (2) searched for a formal mechanism: 'MCIT MALR cooperation protocol committee', Arabic equivalents — no decree or standing joint committee found; (3) T5 press (agrinewz, elwatan) reviewed for leads only.
cells.notes: Prior desk pass recorded 'MALR-MCIT joint project reviews (SIS, Zawya)' at level 4 and prerequisite status Present. Verified: the cooperation is real, recurring and productive, but it is a de facto mechanism — no formal standing body was found. If the DELIVERY prerequisite requires a constituted standing committee, the honest reading is Absent (formal) / Operating (de facto); recorded Operating with this caveat explicit.
cells.protocol_issues: Indicator definition ambiguity flagged for the defect log: 'standing body/committee' vs 'documented recurring coordination mechanism' — Egypt passes the second, not verifiably the first. The presence rung chosen (Operating) follows substance over form; the spec should state which reading governs the DELIVERY flag.

bundle_issues: 1) ITU DataHub returned HTTP 403 to every access route (direct fetch, API, in-browser session) on 2026-08-22 — any bundle relying on DataHub for exact ITU values (GCI overall score, prices, coverage) currently cannot resolve them; GCI 2024 itself publishes tier bands only, so exact per-country scores must come from regulator announcements (T3). 2) Scale mismatch in the spec: indicator 4.2 is defined 0-1 while ITU publishes GCI 0-100 — normalisation convention needs to be fixed centrally. 3) Oxford Insights gates its Index Data behind a registration form and stopped printing overall country scores in the 2025 report annex — the press-circulated 57.5 for Egypt is not openly verifiable; scored the verifiable 2024 figure (55.63) instead (same threshold band). 4) Egyptian T3 legal artefacts (Official Gazette, PDPC site) lack stable public deep links; legal presence facts for the PDPL Executive Regulations rest on archived full-text law-firm analyses (T4) — a tier-assignment judgement call flagged per spec 13.6. 5) Wayback captures were requested (HTTP 302 accepted) for all cited T4 deep links on 2026-08-22. 6) The C3 cluster has moved materially since the v1.6 desk pass: PDPL executive regulations issued Nov 2025 (prior's stale flag resolved), digital ID refreshed to a 2024 T1 observation (98.8, correcting a prior mis-read of 97.2), and the GAIRI 2025 edition published — downstream pillar arithmetic should be re-run. 7) sis.gov.eg presents a TLS certificate-chain issue for automated fetchers (content retrieved with verification relaxed); links resolve normally in browsers.
